title: Analytics Pipeline — Event Lifecycle
purpose: Document the analytics event lifecycle from user action through logging, storage, RPC increment, and consumption by creator/admin dashboards
audience: Backend developers, data engineers, product managers, performance engineers
description: The analytics pipeline captures user engagement events (profile visits, post views, gallery adds, tips) sent from the frontend to POST /api/v1/analytics/log with optionalProtect middleware (allows anonymous/guest users). The controller validates the event type against a known enum, then the service checks if the viewer is admin or the content creator (skips self-views). Events are inserted into the analytics_events table with viewer_id (nullable for guests), event_type, target_id, and metadata. For post_view events, a PostgreSQL RPC increment_content_view_count is called to update content.stats.views JSONB. Data consumers include the creator dashboard (countEventsForCreator with COUNT(*) queries) and admin dashboard (getDashboardStats with 5 parallel queries). Critical gaps: no data aggregation/caching (raw COUNT(*) on full table per load), unbounded table growth (no TTL, archive, or deletion policy), and guest tracking with nullable viewer_id.

preconditions: User is performing an action on the platform (viewing content, visiting profile, adding to gallery)
Frontend has implemented analytics tracking for the relevant user actions
analytics_events table exists with proper schema
PostgreSQL RPC functions (increment_content_view_count, etc.) are installed
postconditions: Event record persisted in analytics_events table with viewer_id (nullable for guests)
For post_view events: content.stats.views incremented by 1
Dashboard queries return aggregated counts via COUNT(*) queries

nodes.label: User Action Triggers Event
nodes.description: User views content, visits profile, adds to gallery, or sends tip. Frontend prepares analytics payload.

nodes.label: Frontend POST /api/v1/analytics/log
nodes.description: Frontend sends HTTP POST with { eventType, creatorId, contentId?, metadata? }.

nodes.label: optionalProtect Middleware
nodes.description: Optional JWT check — attaches req.user if valid token present; does NOT reject unauthenticated requests. Guest users have req.user = null.

nodes.label: Analytics Controller — Validate Event Type
nodes.description: Check eventType is one of known enum values (profile_visit, post_view, gallery_add, tip). Return 400 if invalid.

nodes.label: Analytics Service — logAnalyticsEvent()
nodes.description: Entry into service layer for processing the analytics event.

nodes.label: Fetch Viewer Profile (if authenticated)
nodes.description: If viewerId present from JWT, fetch viewer profile to check role for skip logic.

nodes.label: Is Viewer Admin or Content Creator?
nodes.description: Skip event recording if viewer is admin (to avoid inflating stats) or is the content creator viewing own content.

nodes.label: Silently Skip Event
nodes.description: Admin and self-views are silently discarded — no record created.

nodes.label: INSERT into analytics_events
nodes.description: Insert row with viewer_id (nullable), event_type, creator_id, content_id (nullable), created_at.

nodes.label: Check Insert Success
nodes.description: Verify the event record was successfully created in the database.

nodes.label: Return Error Response
nodes.description: If INSERT fails, return AppError(500) to frontend.

nodes.label: Is Event Type 'post_view'?
nodes.description: Check if the event type requires additional RPC processing.

nodes.label: Call Postgres RPC: increment_content_view_count
nodes.description: Execute supabase.rpc('increment_content_view_count', { content_id_to_update: contentId }) to atomically increment content.stats.views.

nodes.label: Complete — Return Success
nodes.description: Return { success: true, message: 'Event logged.' } to frontend.

nodes.label: Creator Dashboard Load
nodes.description: Creator navigates to dashboard → triggers countEventsForCreator queries for analytics.

nodes.label: countEventsForCreator() Query
nodes.description: COUNT(*) query on analytics_events filtered by creator_id, eventType, and date range. Raw scan — no aggregation/caching.

nodes.label: Admin Dashboard Load
nodes.description: Admin navigates to dashboard → getDashboardStats() includes platform-wide analytics counts.

nodes.label: Display Dashboard Analytics
nodes.description: Creator dashboard or admin dashboard renders aggregated analytics data from COUNT(*) results.

validationRules: eventType must be one of: profile_visit, post_view, gallery_add, tip (known enum)
creatorId is required and must be a valid UUID
contentId is optional — required only for post_view and gallery_add events
viewer_id is extracted from JWT if present; null for unauthenticated guests
businessRules: Admin views are silently discarded — no event recorded for admin activity
Self-views (creator viewing own content) are silently discarded
Guest views (unauthenticated) are recorded with viewer_id = null
post_view events trigger atomic RPC increment on content.stats.views
analytics_events is append-only — no modification or deletion
No TTL, archive, or deletion policy — unbounded table growth
securityConsiderations: nullable viewer_id provides guest tracking without PII (no IP/device tracking)
No PII stored in analytics_events — only UUID references to profiles
Admin and creator dashboards expose aggregated data — not individual event details
Unbounded data growth is a GDPR compliance risk (right to erasure)
Guest tracking allows anonymous behavior analysis without consent dialog
performanceConsiderations: No data aggregation/caching — every dashboard load runs raw COUNT(*) on full table
Unbounded table growth — COUNT(*) queries become progressively slower
Creator dashboard runs countEventsForCreator with optional date range filtering — may not use indexes effectively
Admin dashboard runs 5 parallel COUNT(*) queries — risk of Promise.all failure if one query times out
Missing index on (creator_id, event_type, created_at) for frequent dashboard queries

annotations.label: 🔴 No Data Aggregation/Caching
annotations.description: Every dashboard load runs raw COUNT(*) on the full analytics_events table. No pre-computed summaries.

annotations.label: 🔴 Unbounded Table Growth
annotations.description: analytics_events has no TTL, archive, or deletion policy. Data accumulates indefinitely.

annotations.label: 🟡 Guest Tracking
annotations.description: Guest views recorded with viewer_id=null. No privacy consideration documented.

annotations.label: RPC failure is non-blocking
annotations.description: If increment_content_view_count fails, event is still recorded and success returned. View count may drift.
